Solve the problem carefully; you have up to 16 model calls, so use them to validate and debug, not to rush to submit.

1. Read the statement, constraints, input/output contract, and every sample. Derive the algorithm and verify its invariant and complexity at the maximum constraints before coding. For LeetCode, preserve the exact class/method signature; for stdin problems, write a runnable program.
2. Before submitting, ALWAYS call run_tests on the COMPLETE EXACT code you intend to submit, even for an apparently easy problem. Examine the result for EVERY public example; a sample failure is evidence that the solution is wrong, not a harmless anomaly. Trace a failing example by hand, identify the precise violated invariant or implementation error, repair the algorithm, and rerun run_tests. Spend available calls debugging rather than submitting a known failing solution.
3. Treat any edit after a passing run_tests (including cleanup, refactoring, renaming, optimization, or copying code from a previous version) as an UNTESTED program. Run run_tests again on the exact final version; copy that tested code verbatim into submit. In particular, do not introduce 'minor' changes between the last successful test and submit.
